yarn-deadset.meaning: Every point survives, paragraph for paragraph: the opportunity, the talented colleagues and culture, partnering across government, strategic and practical, "open, iterative and user-centred", the invitation "So please let us know if you see any way we can do better", and the thanks.
yarn-deadset.sense: Mostly exact: "fired up", "care heaps", "dead set on working in an open, iterative and user-centred way" for committed, "stoked". "being a good mate to our colleagues" narrows "great partner" to friendship, a slight strain.
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian manager's welcome: "You've just joined a top bunch of people", "We have a red-hot go at not just leading the way in technology".
yarn-deadset.register: Level 3 weight: a steady Aussie layer ("top bunch", "fired up", "red-hot go", "dead set", "stoked") that still reads as a welcome letter; no swearing, which suits it.
yarn-deadset.tone: Warm and upbeat throughout, as in the original: "Thanks again for bringing your talents to serve the public. We’re stoked to have you".
yarn-deadset.flow: Smooth: "How well we work with colleagues across government is crucial to whether we can make a difference."
yarn-deadset.variety: Varied ("top bunch", "fired up", "heaps", "red-hot go", "dead set", "stoked"), with "chance" repeated ("a chance like no other", "That chance is what brings us together").
yarn-deadset.essence: Unmistakably the TTS welcome letter, same shape and sentiments, retold: "We try to be both strategic and practical".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: All points kept: "That chance is what brings us all together", the culture list, "If we can't work with colleagues across government, we can't make a difference, simple as that", agile organisation, the invitation and thanks.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit ("cracking bunch", "red-hot go", "dead set", "give us a yell", "stoked"), but "being a good mate to our colleagues" narrows "partner" to friendship.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural Australian voice: "So if you spot any way we can do better, give us a yell." and "keeping our feet on the ground with the nitty gritty".
yarn-dinkum.register: Right at level 3: conversational Aussie throughout ("cracking bunch", "simple as that", "give us a yell") with one dad-level swear, "bloody talented", within the brief.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Warm and upbeat, but "The people you'll be working with here are bloody talented" puts a swear into an official welcome letter, a slight wobble.
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads as if written that way: "We're having a red-hot go at leading the way in technology, sure, but also at being the modern, collaborative, diverse culture we want to see."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied openers and terms: "Well,", "cracking bunch", "fired up", "heaps", "red-hot go", "simple as that", "dead set", "give us a yell", "stoked".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the welcome letter, same order and sentiments: "Thanks again for putting your talents into serving the public."

unharnessed.meaning: Mostly faithful, but some swaps shift meaning: "transparent" becomes "inclusive, open, respectful and upbeat", "agile" (the methodology) becomes "as nimble and user-focused as our projects", and "unprecedented" becomes "a once-in-a-lifetime chance".
unharnessed.sense: "we try to show off the modern, collaborative, diverse culture" gives "exemplify" the sense of boasting; "nimble" loses the technical sense of "agile". The rest fits: "ripper bunch", "fired up", "give us a yell".
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural on the whole ("ripper bunch", "give us a yell", "We're stoked"), with some generic choices: "a top-notch partner", "seriously inspiring work".
unharnessed.register: Close to level 3, a touch light in the middle paragraphs ("We're committed to working in an open, iterative and user-centred way"); one dad-level swear, "bloody talented", within the brief.
unharnessed.tone: Warm and upbeat, but "bloody talented" in a welcome letter and "show off" (which reads as boastful) wobble it slightly.
unharnessed.flow: Smooth throughout: "Being able to work well with colleagues across government is crucial to us making a difference."
unharnessed.variety: Reasonably varied ("ripper", "seriously", "fired up", "top-notch", "give us a yell", "stoked"), with "try to" repeated ("We don't just try to lead", "we try to show off", "We try to be both").
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the welcome letter, same shape and line breaks, retold: "Thanks again for bringing your talents to serve the public."

engine.meaning: Nearly verbatim, so the points survive, but "our bloody organisation" changes the writer's attitude to the agency from pride to exasperation.
engine.sense: "We aim to make our bloody organisation as agile" reads as annoyance, the opposite of the original's warmth; "a bloody great partner" fits as an intensifier but jars; "dead set on working" fits.
engine.authenticity: Swears dropped into untouched official prose: "We strive not only to lead the way in technology, but to exemplify", with US spelling left: "user-centered".
engine.register: Left largely untranslated: apart from two "bloody"s, "dead set" and "organisation", it is the original word for word ("We have an unprecedented opportunity to bring our government into the digital age").
engine.tone: The warm, inspiring tone is undercut where the swears land: "our bloody organisation" sounds fed up, inverting the pride the line expresses.
engine.flow: The original reads smoothly, but the inserts jar: "being a bloody great partner to our colleagues throughout government", "our bloody organisation".
engine.variety: Only "bloody" (twice) and "dead set": "a bloody great partner", "our bloody organisation", "We are dead set on".
engine.essence: Recognisably the original, since it is nearly unchanged: "You’ve just joined a remarkable group of people doing inspiring work."

yarn-troppo.meaning: The original's points are all there, but new claims and slants are added: "No dragging the chain, no backstabbing, no sour faces.", "dragging our government kicking and screaming into the digital age" (casting government as resisting), and "the ... culture we're always banging on about", which implies talk more than practice.
yarn-troppo.sense: Most terms fit ("cracking bunch", "this mob", "getting particular projects over the line", "give us a yell"), but "banging on about" means to talk tediously, which undercuts "the culture we want to see".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Plenty of real Aussie ("bloody talented and dedicated as", "dragging the chain", "over the line"), but piled on as tags: "Righto.", "Here's the thing.", "We won't bite, promise.
yarn-troppo.register: Far heavier than level 3: a yarn-style welcome with quips on every paragraph ("get anyone off the couch", "Getting stuff out the door, in other words.", "Thanks again ... mate"). Swearing stays within dad level: "bloody talented".
yarn-troppo.tone: Warm, but it wobbles into cheek that sits against an inspiring welcome: "kicking and screaming", "the modern, collaborative, diverse culture we're always banging on about".
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads aloud with energy, but tags stack up: "And we're dead set on working in an open, iterative and user-centred way, with a strong focus on delivery. Getting stuff out the door, in other words."
yarn-troppo.variety: Very varied: "Righto", "cracking bunch", "off the couch", "the whole show", "this mob", "crew", "dragging the chain", "red-hot go", "over the line", "give us a yell".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the welcome letter in shape, but its earnest, inspiring character turns into a cheeky pep talk: "Here's the thing. We've got a shot nobody's had before".

summaries.yarn-deadset: Faithful, natural and warm, pitched right at level 3; only small shading on a couple of terms.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Natural, varied and faithful at level 3; a 'bloody' that slightly roughens the letter and the 'mate' shading are the only marks against it.
summaries.unharnessed: Natural and smooth, but a few swaps shift the sense ('show off', 'nimble', 'open'), and the swear slightly roughens the letter.
summaries.engine: The original almost untouched, with two bolted-on swears, one of which turns pride into exasperation; far under the brief.
summaries.yarn-troppo: Lively and varied with real Aussie, but far over level 3, with invented lines and a couple of slants that undercut the letter's earnestness.
